articles.title: Hesai JT128 vs Livox Mid-360 for outdoor robot LiDAR
articles.excerpt: By the engineering team at YUANZHI ROBOTICS. We design and build sensor payloads for robot dogs, UGVs and drones. Originally published on our site; AI-assisted draft, reviewed by our engineers. Short…
articles.body: By the engineering team at YUANZHI ROBOTICS. We design and build sensor payloads for robot dogs, UGVs and drones. Originally published on our site; AI-assisted draft, reviewed by our engineers. Short answer: The Hesai JT128 has a much taller vertical field of view (189 degrees), so it sees the ground at the robot's feet and overhead, while the Livox Mid-360 (360 by 59 degrees, about 265 g and 6.5 W) is the easier, better-supported choice for mapping with FAST-LIO2 or Point-LIO. Choose the Mid-360 for mapping and patrol on a robot dog; consider the JT128 when you need curb, step and overhang coverage from one sensor and can supply your own IMU. For outdoor robots the choice between the Hesai JT128 and the Livox Mid-360 comes down to what you need the LiDAR to see.
articles.author: YUANZHI ROBOTICS

articles.body: 做一個線上寺院，技術上不難：建模、貼圖、光影、第一人稱移動，這些都有成熟做法。難的是另一件事—— 節奏 。 實體廟宇之所以讓人靜下來，不是因為它有香爐，而是因為它安排了你的動作順序：進山門、洗手、點香、走到殿前、合掌、低頭、起身，最後才是「求」的那一句。線上版本如果只保留最後一步（點一下求籤），那它得到的就是一個求籤按鈕，不是一座寺院。 一、距離要留著，但不能太長 第一個要做的決定是「走多遠」。 太短，人不會意識到自己正在進入一個不同的地方；太長，人會煩，會想辦法繞過去。寒露寺的院子裡有三十多座殿堂樓閣，從山門到大雄寶殿要走過一段青石板路——不長，剛好夠你把注意力從上一個分頁切換過來。 這裡有一個常被忽略的設計點： 移動本身就是一種儀式 。在很多線上空間裡，移動只是抵達的手段，所以被做得越快越好；但在寺院這種題材裡，移動是內容的一部分。 二、三次禮拜：比一次有份量，比十次不打擾 禮拜的次數是第二個決定。 一次太輕，像按讚；十次太多，會變成苦行，人會中途放棄或直接關掉。三次剛好落在「需要一點決心」和「不需要忍耐」之間。而且三次是有身體感的：合掌、躬身、起身、再來一次——重複會讓人記住自己剛剛做了什麼。 如果把線上參拜設計成「點擊 → 完成 → 獲得反饋」，那它本質上是一個打卡系統；重複三次雖然「低效」，但正是讓人慢下來的地方。 三、一百零八顆念珠：把計數從目標變成過程 念珠是最容易被做成 KPI 的東西。 大部分數位化的念珠會顯示「今日 0 / 108」，撥完跳出鼓勵語。這種設計把念珠變成任務：你要完成它，完成了就該離開。 一百零八顆的念珠在寒露寺裡沒有進度條。你可以撥完整串，也可以只撥幾顆。沒有計數器催你，也沒有「已完成」的提示——撥的動作本身就是目的。這樣的設計在產品指標上幾乎是「反指標」，但它換來的是另一種東西：人願意在裡面待著，而不是急著完成。 四、不求籤也可以：把選…

articles.title: How to Approach Prompt Engineering in Interviews
articles.excerpt: This is a shorter version of a lesson from the AI Engineering course on Aced. The full lesson goes deeper on each technique. Prompt engineering is the work of getting a language model to do a specific…
articles.body: This is a shorter version of a lesson from the AI Engineering course on Aced. The full lesson goes deeper on each technique. Prompt engineering is the work of getting a language model to do a specific task reliably. Most of that work happens after the first draft, when you test the prompt against the inputs it will actually see and revise it based on what goes wrong, much like debugging code. We use one running example throughout: a prompt that turns customer support emails into a structured ticket with a category, an urgency level and a one-line summary. Start with what "good" looks like Before you write anything, define the task and how you will judge the output.
articles.author: Jacob Simon

articles.title: XLOOKUP #N/A "Did not find value" in Google Sheets: confirm the miss, then use if_not_found
articles.excerpt: You type =XLOOKUP(D2,A2:A3,B2:B3) and the cell shows #N/A. Hover it and the tooltip says Did not find value ‘999’ in XLOOKUP evaluation. The function ran. There was no match. That's the same error val…
articles.body: You type =XLOOKUP(D2,A2:A3,B2:B3) and the cell shows #N/A . Hover it and the tooltip says Did not find value ‘999’ in XLOOKUP evaluation. The function ran. There was no match. That's the same error value as a VLOOKUP miss. Confirm the key is actually absent before you change match mode or wrap the formula. Why it happens XLOOKUP defaults to exact match ( match_mode 0). If the search key is not in the lookup range, the result is #N/A . The formula is fine. The key isn't there — or it only looks like it is (a number versus text, or a trailing space). When a miss is a valid result, the fourth argument ( missing_value in Sheets; Excel callers know the same slot as if_not_found ) replaces that #N/A only. A size mismatch, a #REF! range, or #DIV/0! inside a more complex formula still surfaces.

articles.title: The Data Shift Left: Bringing Data Closer to Product Teams
articles.excerpt: Why high-performing product organizations are moving from reactive analytics to embedded data capabilities For years, many organizations have operated with a predictable separation between Product, En…
articles.body: Why high-performing product organizations are moving from reactive analytics to embedded data capabilities For years, many organizations have operated with a predictable separation between Product, Engineering, and Data. Product teams define what to build. Engineering builds it. Data teams collect the information, prepare dashboards, and eventually explain what happened. This model creates a fundamental problem: data becomes involved after the most important product decisions have already been made. By the time an analyst receives a request to measure a new feature, the tracking may not exist. The business hypothesis may not have been clearly defined. The relevant metrics may be inconsistent across dashboards. And the opportunity to design a meaningful experiment may already be gone.

articles.body: The graphics in GTA 6 are so realistic that actual photos and videos are being mistaken as screenshots or clips from the game. It feels like every social media platform is chock-full of posts about Rockstar’s latest release, which has cemented itself as the biggest entertainment launch of all time . Everybody’s talking about it; it’s practically impossible to scroll through your timeline without seeing it in some form or another. GTA 6 is a good-looking game, to say the least, with some of the most realistic visuals we’ve seen in a digital world thus far — to the point where it’s genuinely hard to tell the difference between what’s from the game and what’s from real life.

articles.body: Credit: NASA NASA, on behalf of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), has awarded a contract to Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation for the Sounder for Microwave-Based Applications (SMBA) instruments on NOAA’s Near Earth Orbit Network (NEON) satellites. The cost-plus-fixed-fee, firm-fixed-price, and time-and-materials hybrid contract has a value of $290.6 million. The period of performance runs from Nov. 23 through April 1, 2042. The work will take place at the awardee’s facility. Under the contract, Northrop Grumman will provide the design, development, production, testing, and mission support for three SMBA instruments, the next generation of low Earth orbit microwave sounders.

articles.title: How sci‑fi imagines sports in microgravity, and how zero‑g sports might actually work
articles.excerpt: How realistic are the zero-g sports we see in sci-fi? We talk to Les Johnson, former Chief Technologist for NASA, to find out.
articles.body: Sports in space have a long and proud tradition, whether it's Alan Shepard playing golf on the moon or the crew of the ISS hosting their own version of the Summer Olympics . The future looks bright as well, with the foundation of the Space Games Federation , the self-described "first governing and sanctioning body for competitive sports played in zero or micro-gravity," co-founded by a NASA astronaut. Not to be outdone, science fiction has expanded the idea of zero-g and low-gravity sports to their logical extent, imagining everything from Doctor Who's zero-g squash to the advanced, gamified combat simulations of Ender's Game.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 23, 2015: Blue Origin sticks 1st-ever rocket landing from space with its suborbital New Shepard rocket
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 23, 2015, a Blue Origin rocket made a historic landing after launching into suborbital space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 23, 2015, a Blue Origin rocket made a historic landing. Before this time, all rockets were single-use only — even SpaceX's rockets. Blue Origin changed the concept forever. After launching the New Shepard capsule safely into space, the rocket started heading back to Earth. It flew towards a landing pad, reignited its engine to slow down and touched down softly on the ground . This was the first successful vertical landing from space in history. The Blue Origin milestone meant that rockets could be reused for multiple missions, which saves money and reduces waste. (Image credit: Blue Origin) Why it mattered Today, SpaceX may be the most well-known for landing its Falcon 9 rocket boosters from orbit.

articles.excerpt: This Nov. 19, 2026, image shows gastric microtumors grown within an Encapsulates biochip. The Encapsulate-1 investigation studies patient-derived tumor samples aboard the International Space Station t…
articles.body: Encapsulate Inc. This Nov. 19, 2026, image shows gastric microtumors grown within an Encapsulates biochip. The Encapsulate-1 investigation studies patient-derived tumor samples aboard the International Space Station to better understand how cancer cells move and interact in microgravity. The results could help researchers develop further testing to predict a patient’s risk of metastasis and support more personalized cancer treatments. Orbiting more than 200 miles (320 km) above Earth, the space station is a powerhouse of cutting-edge science that is unlocking discoveries not possible on Earth. Image credit: Encapsulate Inc.
